'''Lavoy Allen''' (born February 4, 1989 in [[Morrisville, Pennsylvania]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player with the [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple Owls men's basketball team]] who has completed his [[2010–11 Temple Owls men's basketball team|senior season]]. Allen is the son of a truck driver, and did not play much basketball until eighth grade. He attended [[Pennsbury High School]], where he was coached by Frank Sciolla. [[Rivals.com]] ranked him the 14th best center in his class, and [[Scout.com]] named him the 110th overall prospect. Allen comitted to [[Temple University]] and coach [[Fran Dunphy]].

Temple reached the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] in all four seasons that Allen played there. He was a three-time All-Atlantic 10 Defensive Team honoree and a two-time All-Atlantic 10 First Team recipient. In his junior year, he became the first Temple player to average a double-double since [[Ollie Johnson]] accomplished the feat in 1970-71. Allen declared for early entry in the [[2010 NBA Draft]], but withdrew prior to the May 8 deadine. As a senior, Allen surpassed [[Johnny Baum]] as the all-time leading rebounder in Temple history. He was the recipient of the [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy]] honoring the [[Philadelphia Big Five]] Player of the Year. Dunphy has said that Allen "might be the smartest player I've ever coached."<ref name=NewHeights/>

==Early life==
Allen was born in the Philadelphia suburb of [[Morrisville, Pennsylvania]] on February 4, 1989.<ref name=NewHeights>{{cite news|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/20100309_Lavoy_Allen_taking_Temple_to_new_heights.html|title=Lavoy Allen taking Temple to new heights|first=Mike|last=Jensen|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=March 9, 2010|accessdate=December 24, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/prospects/lavoy-allen/|title=Prospect profile: Lavoy Allen|first=Chris|last=Dortch|work=[[NBA]]|publisher=NBA Media Ventures|accessdate=June 1, 2011}}</ref> His mother is Paula Allen and his father, Dave Allen, is a truck driver. As a child, Lavoy did not play much organized basketball until eighth grade. In an interview, he admitted he was not very good in the beginning, and focused on passing the ball to a better teammate.<ref name=NewHeights/> His initial motivation was how schoolchildren mocked him for his height yet not being able to dunk.<ref name=Spectacular>{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-01-31/sports/27092178_1_middle-school-frank-sciolla-voluntary-workouts|title=Temple's Lavoy Allen has quietly had a spectacular career|first=Dick|last=Jerardi|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=January 31, 2011|accessdate=June 5, 2011}}</ref> 

==High school career==
He attended [[Pennsbury High School]], where he was coached by Frank Sciolla.<ref name=NewHeights/> Current [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]] player Dalton Pepper was his high school teammate.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.buckslocalnews.com/articles/2011/06/02/bucks_sports/doc4de7e696b52c3746190495.txt|title=Levittown’s Dalton  Pepper has transferred to Temple University|first=Steve|last=Sherman|work=[[Bucks Local News]]|date=June 2, 2011|accessdate=June 5, 2011}}</ref> In ninth grade, Allen decided that he wanted to be great, and put in much more practice time.<ref name=NewHeights/> He became a starter on the varsity team in his sophomore year.<ref name=Spectacular/> As a junior, he averaged 12 points and nine rebounds per game, and was named a Top 150 player in his class by Hoop Scoop.<ref name=TempleBio>{{cite web|url=http://www.owlsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4594&path=mbball|title=2010-11 Men's Basketball Roster: #24 Lavoy Allen|work=[[Temple Owls]]|publisher=[[Temple University]]|accessdate=December 25, 2010}}</ref>

In his senior season, Allen posted per-game averages of 13.0 points, 9.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 3.0 blocks, and 2.0 steals.<ref name=TempleBio/> Under Allen, Pennsbury reached the second round of the [[PIAA]] playoffs before losing to [[Harrisburg High School]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P3-1290745271.html|title=Allen to try out for Team USA |first=Jason|last=Haslem|work=[[Bucks County Courier Times]]|date=June 9, 2007|accessdate=December 25, 2010}}</ref> He was named to the Second Team all-Southeastern Pennsylvania at the conclusion of the season. Allen tried out for the USA U-19 basketball team, but did not make the final cut. [[Rivals.com]] ranked him the 14th best center in his class, and [[Scout.com]] named him the 110th overall prospect.<ref name=TempleBio/> On November 8, 2006, Allen committed to Temple, over Division I scholarship offers from [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]], and [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-154062540.html|title=Pennsbury's Allen selects Temple |first=Mike|last=Jensen|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=November 8, 2006|accessdate=December 25, 2010}}</ref> Along with [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] signee [[Chris Wright (basketball, born 1988)|Chris Wright]], Allen was one of two ESPN 100 prospects in the class of 2008 to sign with an [[Atlantic 10]] program.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/notebook?page=notebook/shootaround/atlantic10|title=A-10 ShootAround: Looking for more national attention|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=August 6, 2008|accessdate=December 27, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman===
Coming into his freshman season, Allen was chosen to the Preseason All-Atlantic 10 Rookie Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102407aaa.html|title=Xavier Tabbed To Capture A-10 Men's Basketball Title|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=October 24, 2007|accessdate=December 26, 2010}}</ref> He was seen as an answer for Temple's rebounding and interior scoring struggles from the previous 12-18 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/11/sports/ncaabasketball/11temple.html?ref=ncaabasketball|title=High-Scoring Temple Seeks Defensive Edge|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[The New York Times]]|publisher=[[The New York Times Company]]|date=November 11, 2007|accessdate=December 26, 2010}}</ref> In his first college basketball game, Allen scored eight points and grabbed nine rebounds in a loss to #7 [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]]. From November 18 through December 9, 2007, he scored in double figures in six consecutive games.<ref name=TempleBio/> On February 10, 2008, Allen's season-high 20 points led Temple to a 80-70 overtime victory over the [[UMass Minutemen men's basketball|UMass Minutemen]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280410218|title=Temple 80, Massachusetts 70
|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 10, 2008|accessdate=December 26, 2010}}</ref> Allen was benched in the February 17 game against [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] due to missing a study assignment.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=PI&s_site=philly&p_multi=PI&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=11EE024B2C2ABB70&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|title=Benched player and botched D hurt Owls|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|format=Subscription required|date=February 17, 2008|accessdate=December 28, 2010}}</ref>

The Owls finished the season 21-13, and made the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] for the first time since 2001, receiving a 12 seed by the selection committee. In the first round, they bowed out to fifth-seeded [[2007-08 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 72-61.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000019|title=Michigan State's wealth of balance puts Temple on ice|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 20, 2008|accessdate=December 27, 2010}}</ref> In that game, Allen notched his first [[double-double]] of 13 points and 11 rebounds, and also drained his first two collegiate [[three-pointers]]. He led the team in blocks with a total of 52, and finished second in field goal percentage (.558), third in rebounds per game (5.7), and fourth in points per game (8.1). Allen was selected to the All-Atlantic 10 Rookie Team.<ref name=TempleBio/>

===Sophomore===
As a sophomore, Allen increased his scoring average to 10.9 points per game, second on the team, and again led the team in blocks, with 1.56 per game. He shot .579 from the floor, best from Temple, and his .618 mark in league games led the Atlantic 10. In addition, he led the team and finished third in the Atlantic 10 in rebounding with 9.0 rebounds per game. He had 14 double-doubles on the season. In the Owls' game against [[Lafayette Leopards|Lafayette]], Allen broke his thumb and was forced to miss the next game, against [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]].<ref name=TempleBio/> His season-high 23 points came on February 8, when the Owls defeated the [[Rhode Island Rams]] 68-62; Allen also had 13 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290390218|title=Temple 68, Rhode Island 62|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 8, 2009|accessdate=December 27, 2010}}</ref> The following day, Allen received his first [[Philadelphia Big 5]] player of the week honors. He would again be honored as Big 5 player of the week on February 23,<ref name=TempleBio/> following a 20-point and season-high 18 rebound performance against [[St. Bonaventure]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290530218|title=Temple 70, St. Bonaventure 56|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 22, 2009|accessdate=December 28, 2010}}</ref>

At the end of the regular season, Allen was named to the All-Atlantic 10 Third Team and All-Atlantic 10 Defensive Team.<ref name=TempleBio/> He helped Temple to its second consecutive Atlantic 10 Tournament title and NCAA Tournament appearance. In the championship game over [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], Allen contributed 10 points and 14 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290730218|title=Christmas scores 29 points; Temple ends Duquesne's dreams of return to NCAA|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 14, 2009|accessdate=January 11, 2011}}</ref> He posted 10 points and 11 rebounds against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] in an [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]] Round of 64 loss.<ref name=TempleBio/>

===Junior===
Allen was a Preseason All-Atlantic 10 First Team selection in his junior year.<ref name=preseasonallconf>{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/MBBPre0910.pdf|title=2009-10 Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Preseason All-Conference Teams|date=October 22, 2009|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|accessdate= December 18, 2009}}</ref> He averaged 11.5 points and 10.7 rebounds per game, becoming the first Temple player to average a double-double since [[Ollie Johnson]] accomplished the feat in 1970-71.<ref name=DeclareDraft>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5131161|title=Allen declares for draft|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=April 23, 2010|accessdate=January 2, 2011}}</ref> Allen's 10.9 rebounds per game average in Atlantic 10 conference games was bested only by [[Fordham Rams|Fordham]]'s [[Chris Gaston]] and [[2009–10 Duquesne Dukes men's basketball team|Duquesne]]'s [[Damian Saunders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/3/stat/rebounds/sort/avgRebounds/year/2010/atlantic-10-conference|title=Atlantic 10 Team Rebounds Statistics - 2009-10|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|accessdate=April 28, 2011}}</ref> In addition, he led Temple in field goal percentage at .536.<ref name=TempleBio/> He scored 10 points and snatched 17 rebounds in the Owls' upset of #3 [[2009–10 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] on December 19.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293470218|title=Fernandez drains 7 3-pointers to help Temple stun Villanova
|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 13, 2009|accessdate=April 28, 2011}}</ref> In a 65-53 win over La Salle on February 28, 2010, Allen scored 17 points and grabbed 21 rebounds,<ref name=message>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300592325|title=Fernandez scores 23; Allen has 17 points, 21 rebounds as Temple sends message|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 28, 2010|accessdate=April 29, 2011}}</ref> a career high and the most by an Owl since [[Joe Newman (basketball player)|Joe Newman]] pulled down 24 on February 5, 1973.<ref name=TempleBio/> With the victory, Temple clinched the Philadelphia Big Five title with a perfect 4-0 record.<ref name=message/> Allen became the 46th Temple player to score 1,000 points in his career in a game against [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]]. This earned him Atlantic 10 (co-)player of the week honors for the week of March 7.<ref name=TempleBio/>

Led by Allen, Temple enjoyed a 29-5 season, captured a share of the Atlantic 10 conference regular season championship with a 14-2 record, and culminated in a third consecutive [[2010 Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Tournament|Atlantic 10 conference tournament]] title and an automatic bid to the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300730218|title=Temple holds off Richmond rally to claim another A-10 championship|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 14, 2010|accessdate=April 29, 2011}}</ref> In the NCAA Tournament, Temple was seeded fifth and matched up with 12 seed [[2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team|Cornell]] in the first round. Allen had 11 points, but his Owls were upset by the Big Red 78-65.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300780218|title=Cornell builds big lead, dominates Temple in first-round upset
|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 19, 2010|accessdate=April 30, 2011}}</ref> Following the season, Allen was selected to the All-Atlantic 10 First Team and All-Atlantic 10 Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030710aab.html|title=A-10 Announces Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|date=March 7, 2010|accessdate=April 29, 2011}}</ref> He was recognized as an All-Fourth District first-team selection by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] making him eligible for the State Farm Division I All‐America teams.<ref>{{cite web
| url=http://www.nabc.org/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/nabc/genrel/auto_pdf/2010D1All-District|format=PDF| work=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]| title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces 2010 Division I All-District Teams | accessdate=April 30, 2011|date=March 16, 2010}}</ref> Since the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] was its own district, this is equivalent to being named first team All-Atlantic 10 by the NABC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nabc.org/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/nabc/genrel/auto_pdf/D1Districts|title=2009–10 NABC Division I District Alignment|accessdate=April 30, 2011|work=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]}}</ref> The [[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] named Allen to the 10-man All-District II team covering college basketball players in the states of New York, New Jersey, Delaware. the District of Columbia, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2010/alldistrict100309.html|work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]]|title=USBWA Names 2009–10 Men's All-District Teams| accessdate=May 8, 2011|date=March 9, 2010}}</ref>

Allen briefly flirted with the [[2010 NBA Draft]]. He declared for early entry in the draft, but did not hire an [[sports agent|agent]].<ref name=DeclareDraft/> After one workout with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Allen was told to return to school to work on his offensive game.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ted|last=Keith|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1177621/index.htm|title=20 Temple Owls|accessdate=April 30, 2011|date=November 22, 2010|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Time Inc.]]}}</ref> On May 8, Allen officially pulled his name out of consideration for the draft. He did so on the final day allowed by the NCAA to ensure collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|first=Keith|last=Tatum|url=http://articles.philly.com/2010-05-09/sports/24958523_1_owls-lavoy-allen-temple|title=Lavoy Allen out of NBA draft|accessdate=April 30, 2011|date=May 9, 2010|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com}}</ref>

===Senior===
Allen was named to the 20-man USA Select team, which played with and against the USA National team from July 19-24.<ref>{{cite news|first=Phil|last=Jasner|url=http://articles.philly.com/2010-07-09/sports/24967473_1_76ers-andre-iguodala-nate-mcmillan-duke-s-mike-krzyzewski|title=Temple's Allen, other locals to play for USA select team|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=July 9, 2010 |accessdate=April 30, 2011}}</ref> Prior to his senior campaign, he was on the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] watchlists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=861|title=2010-2011 Men’s Preseason Top 50 List|work=[[John R. Wooden Award]]|accessdate=November 12, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.owlsports.com/news/2010/11/16/MBB_1116103924.aspx|title=Lavoy Allen Named To Naismith Preseason Watch List|accessdate=November 17, 2010|date=November 16, 2010|work=[[Temple Owls]]|publisher=[[Temple University]]}}</ref> He was a preseason All-Atlantic 10 First Team and Defensive Team selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102110aaa.html|title=Temple Tabbed A-10 Favorites; League Announces Preseason Accolades|date=October 21, 2010|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=November 12, 2010}}</ref> On December 6, Allen was named Atlantic 10 co-player of the week after recording back-to back double-doubles against [[Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball|Central Michigan]] and [[2010–11 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], both Temple victories.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/120610aac.html|title=Atlantic 10 Announces Men's Basketball Player And Rookie Of The Week|date=December 6, 2010|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=December 9, 2010}}</ref> He sprained his ankle in a game against [[Fordham Rams|Fordham]] on February 9, 2011, and was forced to miss the following game, versus the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]].<ref>{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310432168|title=Temple Owls' defense pressures Dayton to 37 percent shooting|accessdate=March 29, 2011|date=February 12, 2011|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}}</ref> In the February 20 game against [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]], Allen became Temple's all time leader in rebounds. Allen snatched 12 boards to pass Temple radio analyst [[Johnny Baum]]'s career 1,042 rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310510218|title=No. 25 Temple cruises past city-rival St. Joseph's|accessdate=March 30, 2011|date=February 20, 2011|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}}</ref> He received conference player of the week honors for the week of February 28.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022811aaa.html|title=Atlantic 10 Announces Men's Basketball Player And Rookie Of The Week|date=February 28, 2011|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=March 6, 2011}}</ref> Allen scored a career-high 24 points to top [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] in the regular season finale, earning him Atlantic 10 Player of the Week recognition on March 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030611aab.html|title=Atlantic 10 Announces Final Men's Basketball Player And Rookie Of The Week Of The Season|date=March 6, 2011|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=March 7, 2011}}</ref>

Temple finished with a 26–8 record in Allen's senior season and earned a berth to the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. This time, they defeated [[2010–11 Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball team|Penn State]] in the Round of 64 before falling to [[2010–11 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]] in double overtime. Allen had 12 points and 11 rebounds in his final game as a Temple Owl.<ref>{{cite news|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310780021|title=San Diego State needs two overtimes to put away Temple|accessdate=April 8, 2011|date=March 19, 2011|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}}</ref> He was named to the All-Atlantic 10 First Team and Defensive Team at the conclusion of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2010-11all-conferencehonors|title=2010-11 Atlantic 10 Conference Men’s Basketball All-Conference Teams|format=PDF|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|accessdate=March 23, 2011}}</ref> Allen was the recipient of the [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy]] honoring the [[Philadelphia Big Five]] Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philadelphiabig5.org/newsfull.php?Big-5-Announces-2010-2011-Men-s-Basketball-Award-Winners-151|title=Big 5 Announces 2010-11 Men's Basketball Award Winners|work=[[Philadelphia Big Five]]|date=April 13, 2011|accessdate=April 13, 2011}}</ref>

Behind Chris Gaston of Fordham, Allen finished second in conference in rebounding average with a 8.4 mark in league play,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/3/stat/rebounds/sort/avgRebounds/year/2011/atlantic-10-conference|title=Atlantic 10 Team Rebounds Statistics - 2010-11|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|accessdate=April 28, 2011}}</ref> and was fifth in the Atlantic 10 in blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/3/stat/blocks/sort/avgBlocks/year/2011/atlantic-10-conference|title=Atlantic 10 Team Blocks Statistics - 2010-11|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|accessdate=April 28, 2011}}</ref> In addition, he averaged 11.6 points per game, second on the team.<ref name=stats/> For his career, he pulled down 1,147 rebounds and scored 1,421 points, 24th in Temple history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.owlsports.com/news/2011/4/6/MBB_0406115152.aspx|title=Lavoy Allen Named Men's Basketball Most Valuable Player|work=[[Temple Owls]]|publisher=[[Temple University]]|date=April 6, 2011|accessdate=June 1, 2011}}</ref> Temple coach [[Fran Dunphy]] has said that Allen "might be the smartest player I've ever coached in terms of positioning and understanding the game - just his knowledge."<ref name=NewHeights/>

==Professional career==
On April 1, 2011, Allen participated in the 2011 Reese's College All-Star game held at the [[Reliant Center]] in [[Houston, Texas]]. He contributed 11 points and eight rebounds as his East team lost to the West 113-108.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.owlsports.com/news/2011/4/1/MBB_0401113812.aspx|title=Lavoy Allen Scores 11 Points in Reese's College All-Star Game|work=[[Temple Owls]]|publisher=[[Temple University]]|date=April 1, 2011|accessdate=June 1, 2011}}</ref> [[Chad Ford]] of ESPN said that Allen was the 99th best prospect in the [[2011 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Ford|url=http://m.espn.go.com/nba/story?storyId=6554694&pg=0|title=Chad Ford's Top 100|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=May 15, 2011|accessdate=June 1, 2011}}</ref> Allen sprained his ankle in a workout with his hometown [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and was forced to miss the next workout with the [[New Jersey Nets]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Tom|last=Canavan|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-06-06-2747716333_x.htm|title=Allen misses Nets' workout because of ankle injury|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[USA Today]]|date=June 6, 2011|accessdate=June 7, 2011}}</ref>
